Journalist Curt Mills joins Tucker Carlson to argue that Donald Trump can save America or wage a new war, but not both. The episode title lays Mills's fork in the road bare. Mills writes on foreign policy from the right.

Mills lays out the two paths as he sees them: a turn home to fix the land, or a new war that eats the term. He names the men who push each path in Trump's ear. Carlson weighs the odds with him. Listeners get a sharp brief on a choice that will shape the age. The library keeps the talk as a record of his stated view.

Müller lays out his charge: the West lost its faith, and with it its nerve and its young. He calls for a return to truth, prayer, and clear moral law. uslaw-usc-t2-s149a:
Section 149a of Title 2 of the United States Code lets the Library of Congress sell surplus property and keep the proceeds. The Librarian of Congress is the officer named. The rule sits in the chapter on the Library of Congress.

Within the limits of money already appropriated, the Librarian may dispose of surplus or obsolete personal property. The allowed routes include transfer to another agency, donation, sale, and trade-in. Amounts received are credited to the funds available for the library's operations. They may be used to acquire the same or similar property in its place. The section lets the library turn dead stock into fresh stock without new appropriations.
uslaw-usc-t2-s29a:
Section 29a of Title 2 of the United States Code deals with early party meets in the House. In any even-numbered year, a party leader may call such a meet. The leader may be the majority leader or the minority leader. The call comes after talks with the Speaker of the House.

The meet brings old Members who won again together with new Members-elect. All must be of the leader's own party in the House. Its aim is to take each step to set the party up fast. The set-up is for the Congress that is about to begin its term. The leader must file a writ notice with the Clerk of the House. The notice gives the date on which the meet is to sit. The Clerk then sends each Member-elect a copy of the notice.
